title: Robot Swarm Maze Pathfinding
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) and GLTFLoader that implements a robot swarm navigating an obstacle maze with A*-inspired pathfinding.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 25, 30) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Renderer should have antialiasing, shadow maps, and fill the viewport.
- Create a ground plane (40x40 units) at y=0 with a dark grid-textured MeshStandardMaterial.

## Asset Loading
- Load 'Parrot.glb' using GLTFLoader. Clone this model 5 times to create a swarm of 5 'robot parrots' (the swarm agents). Scale each to (0.02, 0.02, 0.02). Place them at the START zone: randomly distributed within x:[-18,-16], z:[-18,-16], y:0.5. Tint each clone a unique color using material.color.set (red, blue, green, yellow, cyan). If the model has AnimationMixer animations, play them.
- Load 'ChronographWatch.glb'. Scale it to (40, 40, 40). Place it at the GOAL zone center (17, 1.5, 17). This is the target all swarm agents navigate toward. Rotate it slowly on Y axis.

## Maze / Obstacles
- Procedurally generate a grid-based maze on the 40x40 ground. Use a 20x20 logical grid (each cell = 2x2 world units), offset so grid covers -20 to +20 on x and z. Use a simple recursive backtracker or randomized DFS to carve a maze. Ensure the cell at grid (0,0) mapping to world (-19,-19) and cell (19,19) mapping to world (19,19) are open and connected. Represent walls as BoxGeometry(2, 2, 2) with a gray MeshStandardMaterial, placed at y=1.

## Pathfinding
- Implement A* pathfinding on the 20x20 grid. Each agent computes a path from its nearest grid cell to the goal cell (19,19). Store paths as arrays of grid coordinates.
- Agents move along their computed path at a base speed of 3 units/second. They interpolate smoothly between waypoints. Agents face their movement direction (lookAt next waypoint).
- Implement simple collision avoidance: if two agents are within 1.5 units, apply a small repulsion force perpendicular to their movement direction.

## Simulation Controls
- The simulation starts PAUSED. Add a DOM button with id='startBtn' labeled 'Start Simulation'. Clicking it begins agent movement.
- Add a DOM button with id='resetBtn' labeled 'Reset'. Clicking it returns all agents to their start positions, recomputes paths, and pauses.
- Add a DOM button with id='speedBtn' labeled 'Speed: 1x'. Clicking cycles through 1x, 2x, 4x speed multipliers, updating button text.
- Keyboard 'P' toggles pause/resume mid-simulation.
- Keyboard 'O' toggles obstacle visibility (walls still block pathfinding but become invisible/visible).
- Add a DOM element with id='hud' showing: number of agents that reached the goal, current simulation time (seconds, 1 decimal), current speed multiplier, and simulation state (paused/running).

## Agent Arrival
- When an agent's position is within 1.5 units of the goal (ChronographWatch), mark it as 'arrived'. Stop its movement. Increment the arrived counter. An arrived agent should glow (emissive color boost).

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - `agentCount`: number (5)
  - `agentPositions`: array of {x, y, z} for each agent
  - `agentArrived`: array of 5 booleans
  - `arrivedCount`: number of agents that reached goal
  - `simulationRunning`: boolean
  - `simulationTime`: number (seconds elapsed while running)
  - `speedMultiplier`: number (1, 2, or 4)
  - `obstaclesVisible`: boolean
  - `goalPosition`: {x, y, z} of the watch model
  - `pathLengths`: array of 5 numbers (path length in grid steps for each agent)
  - `mazeWallCount`: number of wall boxes placed
  - `agentSpeeds`: array of 5 numbers (current effective speed of each agent)
  - `modelsLoaded`: { parrot: boolean, watch: boolean }

## Visual Polish
- Add a faint trail line (THREE.Line) behind each agent showing its traveled path, colored to match the agent.
- OrbitControls for camera.
physics_constraints: Agents must stay within the 40x40 ground bounds (x,z in [-20,20]). Agents must not pass through maze walls. Agent positions must be NaN-free at all times. Collision avoidance must prevent agents from overlapping (minimum separation ~1.0 unit when near each other). Speed must be exactly base_speed * speedMultiplier. Simulation time must only advance when running.
